headings.title: Credit agreement defined
headings.reviewNote: Covers definition of credit agreement as an agreement to lend, forbear repayment, extend credit, or make financial accommodations.

headings.title: Writing requirement for debtor actions and defenses
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule barring debtor actions or defenses on credit agreements absent writing, consideration, and stated terms, subject to consumer exceptions.

headings.title: Required boldface warning language and oral deferral exception
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory boldface ten-point statutory notice clause and ninety-day oral deferral exception for consumer credit agreements.

headings.title: Creditor enforcement of security instruments unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Covers preservation of creditor rights to enforce promissory notes, guaranties, mortgages, deeds of trust, or security agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: credit agreement definition, writing bar on debtor actions/defenses, 10-point boldface notice and 90-day consumer oral deferral exception, and preservation of creditor security enforcement.

headings.title: Credit agreement defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines "credit agreement" for section 432.047 as an agreement to lend, forbear repayment, extend credit, or make another financial accommodation.

headings.title: Writing and execution requirement for debtor claims and defenses
headings.reviewNote: Covers bar on debtor actions or defenses regardless of legal theory unless credit agreement is in writing, signed by both parties, and contains consideration.

headings.title: Required commercial boldface notice and consumer credit exemption
headings.reviewNote: Covers required boldface ten-point statutory warning notice and express restriction of section 432.047 to commercial credit agreements only.

headings.title: Creditor enforcement of security instruments unaffected
headings.reviewNote: Preserves creditor enforceability of promissory notes, guaranties, security agreements, deeds of trust, mortgages, and similar instruments creating payment obligations or security interests.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text; aligned subsection 1 and 4 titles with their text by removing "commercial" where the commercial-only restriction appears in subsection 3(2).

headings.title: Scope of Uniform Electronic Transactions Act
headings.reviewNote: Covers applicability of sections 432.200 to 432.295 to electronic records and electronic signatures relating to transactions.

headings.title: Exclusions for wills, trusts, and specified commercial code provisions
headings.reviewNote: Covers exclusion of laws governing wills, codicils, testamentary trusts, and specified uniform commercial code articles from UETA coverage.

headings.title: Applicability to excluded transactions governed by other laws
headings.reviewNote: Covers application of UETA to electronic records or signatures involved in excluded transactions to the extent governed by other laws.

headings.title: Application of other substantive law
headings.reviewNote: States that a transaction subject to sections 432.200 to 432.295 is also subject to other applicable substantive law.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: UETA scope, wills/trusts and UCC exclusions, coverage of excluded transactions under other laws, and revised subsection 4 title from "Subordination" to "Application of other substantive law".

headings.title: No mandatory creation or use of electronic records or signatures
headings.reviewNote: Covers principle that UETA does not require records or signatures to be created, sent, or processed by electronic means.

headings.title: Requirement of mutual agreement to conduct electronic transactions
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement of mutual agreement to conduct transactions electronically, determined from context and conduct.

headings.title: Nonwaivable right to refuse other electronic transactions
headings.reviewNote: Covers nonwaivable right of a party to refuse other transactions by electronic means despite prior agreement.

headings.title: Variation of statutory provisions by agreement
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization to vary statutory effects by mutual agreement and interpretation of standard statutory terms.

headings.title: Determination of legal consequences
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that legal consequences of electronic records or signatures are determined by UETA and other applicable law.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text: voluntary electronic use, mutual agreement requirement, nonwaivable refusal right, variation by agreement, and legal consequence determination.

headings.title: Legal recognition of electronic records and signatures
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against denying legal effect or enforceability to records or signatures solely because they are electronic.

headings.title: Legal recognition of contracts formed using electronic records
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against denying contract enforceability solely because electronic records were used in formation.

headings.title: Electronic records satisfy writing requirements
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that an electronic record satisfies any legal requirement that a record be in writing.

headings.title: Electronic signatures satisfy signature requirements
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that an electronic signature satisfies any legal requirement for a signature.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: legal recognition of electronic records, signatures, and contracts, and satisfaction of statutory writing and signature requirements.

headings.title: Requirement of electronic records capable of retention
headings.reviewNote: Covers satisfaction of written delivery requirements by electronic records capable of retention and printing by the recipient.

headings.title: Compliance with other laws governing posting, display, or transmission
headings.reviewNote: Covers obligation to comply with other laws prescribing specific posting, transmission methods, or formatting.

headings.title: Unenforceability of electronic records when sender inhibits retention
headings.reviewNote: Covers unenforceability of electronic records against recipients where sender inhibits printing or storage capabilities.

headings.title: Limitations on varying retention and mailing requirements by agreement
headings.reviewNote: Covers restrictions on varying statutory retention and mailing requirements by agreement, except where permitted by other law.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: retention-capable electronic delivery, compliance with posting/display/transmission/formatting laws, unenforceability when sender inhibits retention, and limits on variation by agreement.

headings.title: Attribution of electronic records and signatures
headings.reviewNote: Covers attribution of electronic records and signatures to a person based on acts and security procedure efficacy.

headings.title: Determination of legal effect from context and circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Covers determination of legal effect of attributed records or signatures from context, circumstances, and agreements.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: attribution of electronic records and signatures via act or security procedure and determination of legal effect from context and agreement.

headings.title: Retention of electronic records satisfying statutory retention rules
headings.reviewNote: Covers criteria for electronic records to satisfy statutory retention requirements by accurate reflection and accessibility.

headings.title: Exemption for transmission metadata and routing information
headings.reviewNote: Covers exemption of transmission, routing, and communication metadata from record retention mandates.

headings.title: Use of third-party record retention services
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization to satisfy statutory record retention requirements through third-party services.

headings.title: Electronic records satisfy original record requirements
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that properly retained electronic records satisfy legal mandates requiring original records.

headings.title: Electronic retention of checks satisfying check retention laws
headings.reviewNote: Covers satisfaction of check retention requirements by retaining front and back electronic check images.

headings.title: Evidentiary and audit purposes satisfied by electronic retention
headings.reviewNote: Covers satisfaction of evidentiary and audit retention mandates absent subsequent statutory prohibition.

headings.title: Governmental agency authority to specify additional retention rules
headings.reviewNote: Covers preservation of state agency authority to establish additional record retention rules within agency jurisdiction.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text: electronic record retention criteria, transmission-only information exclusion, third-party retention, original-record and check-retention satisfaction, post-August 28, 2003 audit/evidentiary rule, and agency authority.

headings.title: Determination of when electronic records are sent
headings.reviewNote: Covers standard criteria determining when an electronic record is sent, including addressing and system transmission.

headings.title: Determination of when electronic records are received
headings.reviewNote: Covers criteria determining when an electronic record is received upon entering designated processing systems.

headings.title: Physical location of processing system immaterial to receipt
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that the physical location of processing systems does not alter the legal place of receipt.

headings.title: Presumed places of sending and receipt at places of business
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory presumption that electronic records are sent from and received at places of business or residence.

headings.title: Receipt effective without individual awareness
headings.reviewNote: Covers effectiveness of electronic record receipt regardless of whether any individual is aware of the arrival.

headings.title: Electronic acknowledgment establishing receipt but not content match
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that automated electronic acknowledgments establish receipt but do not prove identical content correspondence.

headings.title: Actual knowledge of non-sending or non-receipt governed by other law
headings.reviewNote: Covers application of other law to determine legal consequences when a party knows records were not actually sent or received.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text: default rules for time and place of sending and receipt, system location immateriality, awareness immateriality, electronic acknowledgments, and actual knowledge of non-sending or non-receipt.

headings.title: Transferable record defined
headings.reviewNote: Defines "transferable record" as an electronic record that would be a UCC Article 3 note or Article 7 document if in writing and is expressly agreed by the issuer to be transferable; source footnote notes section 400.7-604 was repealed in 2017.

headings.title: Control of transferable records
headings.reviewNote: Covers standard for establishing legal control over transferable electronic records through reliable transfer systems.

headings.title: System requirements for establishing control of transferable records
headings.reviewNote: Covers six statutory criteria for authoritative copy creation, storage, and unalterable assignment to prove control.

headings.title: Rights and defenses of person in control under commercial code
headings.reviewNote: Treats a person in control as a UCC holder (with equivalent rights and defenses, without delivery, possession, or endorsement); source footnote notes 2017 revisor update of section 400.1-201 subdivision reference from (20) to (21).

headings.title: Obligor rights and defenses under commercial code
headings.reviewNote: Covers reservation of equivalent statutory rights and defenses to obligors under electronic transferable records.

headings.title: Proof of control upon request in enforcement proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Covers duty of party enforcing transferable records to provide reasonable proof of control upon request.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text; noted 2017 repeal of referenced section 400.7-604 in subsection 1 and 2017 revisor subdivision renumbering in subsection 4.
